reproduction_target: Construction of the CABBAGE AMR genotype-phenotype database (>170,750 isolates, >1.7M BioSample-antibiotic entries) entirely by computational aggregation and curation of pre-existing public data. There is NO wet-lab work in this paper: every isolate, every AST measurement and every genome was generated by third parties and is re-used here. The reproduction target decomposes into (1) a literature review extracting genotype-phenotype tables from 89 publications with a >=100-isolate threshold, (2) extraction from nine public databases (Microreact, NARMS, NDARO, PathogenWatch, PATRIC, PubMLST, COMPARE, CDC, NCBI antibiograms), (3) conversion of all run/sample/genome identifiers to BioSample IDs plus metadata back-fill, (4) mapping to 29 standardised fields including antibiotic-name harmonisation against the NCBI antibiogram name list, (5) a multi-stage curation pass (genomic-identifier conflict removal, MIC plausibility filtering, typing-method correction, metadata anomaly removal, de-duplication) that is explicitly PARTLY MANUAL, (6) re-derivation of S/I/R phenotypes from raw measurement values under 2025 CLSI and EUCAST breakpoints using the R AMR package v3.0.0, (7) whole-database consistency checks, (8) assembly/retrieval of genomes via ENA and the AllTheBacteria collaboration, (9) CheckM2 quality filtering (completeness <50 or contamination >5 removed; 1,269 genomes dropped), (10) annotation of every genome with the mettannotator pipeline including AMRFinderPlus, and (11) the descriptive/statistical comparison of CABBAGE resistance frequencies against the ATLAS surveillance dataset (logistic regression OR = 1.6, Fisher exact test with FDR adjustment over 103 pathogen-antibiotic pairs). Code availability is a single in-Methods sentence: 'These files were then processed via custom scripts, available at https://github.com/Leonardini/CABBAGE'. There is no separate Code Availability section.

steps.label: Literature review and extraction of genotype-phenotype tables from publications: inclusion threshold of >=100 sequenced isolates of a WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogen with >=1 drug phenotype (threshold 'adjusted for some pathogens', detail deferred to Supplementary Methods S1.1.1); phenotype tables plus genotype accession numbers manually extracted and standardised into CSV. README maps this to PreprocessAllPapers.R (first search) and PreprocessNewPapers.R (second search), with input tables shipped under SelectedTables/, RemainingTables/, NewTables/. 89 publications, >560k entries. No R version, no package versions for this step

Extraction and parsing of nine public source databases (Microreact, NARMS, NDARO, PathogenWatch, PATRIC, PubMLST, COMPARE, CDC, NCBI antibiograms) plus the ENA/SRA antibiogram search (BioProject PRJNA756559, snapshot file 'Antibiograms_ena_sra-analysis_20221119-2217.csv'). README maps this to PreprocessDatabases.R. Per-database entry counts in Supplementary Tables S2/S3; PATRIC contributes >764k entries. No download/access date stated in the paper prose for any database other than the dated ENA search filename, and no source-database release version is pinned

Genomic identifier resolution: 'all sequencing run IDs, sample IDs, and genome accession IDs were converted to BioSample IDs', with missing genomic fields and missing isolate metadata retrieved using the BioSample ID as the central reference. README maps this to ExtractInfo.R with outputs in AllExtractedGenotypes/, resolved mappings in Mappings/ (*_Mapped.csv, AllMappings*.csv) and per-source logs in ExtractionRecords/. The remote service used for resolution (ENA/EBI accession-mapping endpoints) is not named or versioned in the paper, and no query date is given

Data standardisation to the 29 CABBAGE fields (Table 1): harmonisation of antibiotic names from source abbreviations against 'the name list employed by NCBI antibiograms' (with recourse to paper full text where the abbreviation was ambiguous), numeric-to-categorical phenotype conversion, country names to ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, broth microdilution/macrodilution collapsed to 'broth dilution', host collapsed to 'Homo sapiens' or 'other (non-clinical isolate)'. Prose is explicitly partial - 'Further data standardisation steps include, but are not limited to' - with the full description deferred to Supplementary Methods S1.1.13. README maps merged-table construction to PrepareTables.R, described as 'semi-manual scripts', and NCBI-antibiogram/AMR-package lookup tables to ParseTables.R

Curation pass: exclusion of non-WHO-list pathogens, species renaming (e.g. Salmonella typhimurium -> Salmonella enterica), exclusion of entries whose multiple genomic identifiers resolve to different BioSample IDs, exclusion of multiple BioSample IDs sharing a sequencing run ID (presumed pooled sequencing), removal of MIC values 'inconsistent with standard doubling dilution ranges', correction of typing method + measurement unit for anomalous disc-diffusion/MIC values, metadata anomaly removal (host age 999, collection year 1800), and de-duplication including conflicting Biosample/antibiotic pairs. The paper states explicitly 'Only those entries that were inconsistent or conflicted have been manually curated' and 'manually checked against the original data sources'. Full description deferred to Supplementary Methods S1.1.14. Manual decisions are not recorded as a machine-replayable artifact in the repository listing, so this step is reconstructable rather than exactly public

Re-derivation of updated S/I/R phenotypes from measurement values: 'we incorporated updated phenotypes by applying the current 2025 breakpoint criteria from both CLSI and EUCAST, inferred using the AMR package v3.0.0'. This is the ONLY exactly pinned software version in the entire paper. The breakpoint tables are bundled inside the pinned AMR package release, and ParseTables.R is described in the README as preprocessing 'useful tables from the AMR package'. No R interpreter version, no CRAN snapshot date, no channel/repository pin, so the pin does not reach environment closure and version is capped at 1 (subtier exact_pins_partial)

Final whole-database consistency checks, enumerated by example in prose: 'a testing standard can only be reported in the presence of a phenotype, a platform value should have a corresponding typing method, a measurement unit is required if a measurement value is provided alongside a typing method, and each entry must contain both a Biosample ID as well as either a measurement value or a categorical resistance phenotype'. The list is given as instances ('For instance'), not as the complete check set, and no README script is named as the owner of this stage

Genome sourcing/assembly: 'Genome annotation was conducted on previously submitted genomes to the European Nucleotide Archive or on newly assembled genomes from the AllTheBacteria collaboration'. No assembler is named, no assembly parameters, no AllTheBacteria release/version or accession set, and no rule stating which isolates took the ENA-submitted path versus the newly-assembled path. Assembled genomes are stated to be 'available via the European Nucleotide Archive' but no project/assembly accession is given anywhere in the text

Genome quality assessment with CheckM2: 'Genomes were assessed using CheckM2 with 1,269 genomes filtered due to a completeness score less than 50 or contamination score greater than 5'. Filtering thresholds are fully specified and the discarded count is reported, but no CheckM2 version, no CheckM2 reference-database/DIAMOND-model version, and no invocation script are given

Genome annotation with the mettannotator pipeline including AMR annotation from AMRFinderPlus: 'Each genome in the CABBAGE data set was annotated using the pipeline mettannotator, which includes AMR annotation from AMRFinderPlus, providing a unified and consistent annotation set across all CABBAGE genomes'. mettannotator and AMRFinderPlus are both open pipelines, but no version is given for either, no AMRFinderPlus reference-database release is pinned (this is the classic mutable-reference-DB exposure for AMR gene calls), and no parameters, profile or config are stated. The annotation outputs are the 'AMR genotypes' resource served by the EBI portal

Comparative statistical analysis of CABBAGE against the ATLAS surveillance dataset: 103 shared pathogen-antibiotic pairs restricted to collection years 2004-2023 and to pairs with >=100 entries in both datasets; 'Logistic regression analyses revealed that resistance was significantly more frequent in CABBAGE than in ATLAS (OR = 1.6, p < 0.001)'; per-pair testing by 'Fishers exact test, FDR adjusted p < 0.05' yielding 66 pairs higher in CABBAGE and 29 lower. Filters and tests are well specified, but no analysis or figure script is named in the paper or in the repository README (the README enumerates only extraction/preprocessing scripts plus Replication.R), no software or version is given for the regression/testing, and the ATLAS dataset itself is a third-party resource obtained under registration rather than a paper-stated open accession

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 7/11 computational steps (64%). This paper is unusual in the survey in that the CODE axis is NOT the binding constraint for the database-construction core: a public repository (https://github.com/Leonardini/CABBAGE, R, tagged release 'CABBAGE' published 2026-07-02 as 'Public release to accompany the NAR paper') ships the named extraction/preprocessing scripts (PreprocessAllPapers.R, PreprocessNewPapers.R, PreprocessDatabases.R, ExtractInfo.R, PrepareTables.R, ParseTables.R, Utilities.R), the intermediate data tables (SelectedTables/, RemainingTables/, NewTables/, AllExtractedGenotypes/, Mappings/, ExtractionRecords/) AND an explicit reviewer-facing walkthrough, Replication.R, described as 'a self-contained walkthrough of the pipeline on a small representative subset of sources (two papers, the PATRIC database, and the ENA antibiogram search), intended to help reviewers reproduce key outputs from scratch'. That is materially better artifact hygiene than the survey norm. The binding constraint is instead the VERSION axis: exactly one software version appears anywhere in the paper - the R AMR package v3.0.0 used for 2025 CLSI/EUCAST breakpoint inference - and there is no R interpreter version, no CRAN snapshot or MRAN/Posit date, no renv.lock, no DESCRIPTION, no conda environment and no container in the repository root listing. Consequently every step is capped at version = 1 and no step can reach R-star even in principle at Tier-1. The 4/11 steps that fall to NI are the genome-side and analysis-side steps that sit OUTSIDE the R repository: C8 (assembly via ENA / AllTheBacteria, no assembler, no version, no parameters, no accession), C9 (CheckM2, thresholds excellent but no version), C10 (mettannotator + AMRFinderPlus, no version for either and no AMRFinderPlus reference-DB release - a mutable-reference exposure that directly determines the published 'AMR genotypes' resource), and C11 (the CABBAGE-vs-ATLAS logistic regression / Fisher / FDR analysis, for which no code exists in the repository and whose comparator dataset ATLAS is registration-gated rather than openly accessioned, hence data = 1). Note the Delta-5 symmetry caveat: a static_readiness of 0 under-claims by construction, because Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency specification - here the authors may well have run a fixed R installation, but nothing in the paper or README declares it.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML full text (Abstract; Methods 2.1 Data collection, 2.2 Data standardisation, 2.3 Data curation incl. 2.3.1 genomic and 2.3.2 phenotypic, 2.4 Final processing, 2.5 Genome assembly and annotation, 2.6 Database accessibility; Results 3.1-3.4 for the ATLAS comparison) plus the GitHub landing page and README prose of https://github.com/Leonardini/CABBAGE. Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 11/11 = 100%: this is a pure data-aggregation resource paper with zero wet-lab steps of its own (all isolates, ASTs and sequencing were performed by the third parties whose data is aggregated), so W = 0 and there are no OOS steps. Supplementary Methods S1.1.1, S1.1.13 and S1.1.14 are cited by the paper as holding the full threshold, standardisation and curation specifications; they were NOT retrieved at Stage 1 (the supplementary PDF is a separate 'DC1' asset), so the params scores for C1, C4, C5 and C7 are conservative and could rise on supplementary review. The repository was read at landing-page + README level only; no .R source file was opened, per Stage-1 scope.

gaps.where: Whole paper and whole repository. Version = 0 at steps C8, C9, C10, C11; version capped at 1 at all 11 steps
gaps.missing: Near-total absence of version pinning plus total absence of environment closure. (a) Exactly ONE software version appears in the entire paper: 'the AMR package v3.0.0' (Methods 2.4). CheckM2, mettannotator, AMRFinderPlus, the assembler behind the 'newly assembled genomes from the AllTheBacteria collaboration', and the software used for the logistic regression / Fisher exact / FDR analysis all appear with no version at all. (b) No environment closure of any kind: the repository root contains .gitignore, AMRDataTables.Rproj, CLAUDE.md, README.md, nine .R files and data directories - there is no renv.lock, no DESCRIPTION, no packrat, no conda/mamba environment.yml, no lockfile, no Dockerfile, no container digest, no sessionInfo() dump. The R interpreter version is stated nowhere. Under the v0.2.5 symmetric env-closure gate the single AMR v3.0.0 pin is therefore exact_pins_partial and version stays at 1 wherever it is credited, which is what forbids R-star for this paper at Tier-1 and makes it a non-candidate for Stage 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Add renv (renv.lock committed at the release tag) or a Rocker/Bioconductor container with a recorded digest, covering the R interpreter version, the CRAN snapshot date and every package the nine scripts library(). Separately, add a versions table naming exact versions for CheckM2, mettannotator, AMRFinderPlus (tool version AND reference-database release), the assembly pipeline / AllTheBacteria release used, and the statistical toolchain behind Figure 4b.

gaps.where: Step C10 (AMRFinderPlus reference database inside mettannotator); secondarily C9 (CheckM2 reference model) and C2 (source database snapshots)
gaps.missing: The 'AMR genotypes' half of the published resource is produced by AMRFinderPlus running inside mettannotator, and neither the AMRFinderPlus software version nor its reference-database release date is recorded anywhere in the paper. AMRFinderPlus gene calls change materially between database releases, so the published genotype table is not re-derivable to a fixed target. Likewise CheckM2's model/reference bundle is unpinned even though its output removed 1,269 genomes, and the nine source databases (PATRIC, NDARO, NARMS, CDC, PubMLST, PathogenWatch, Microreact, COMPARE, NCBI antibiograms) are all rolling resources harvested with no stated access date - only the ENA/SRA antibiogram search carries a de facto timestamp, via the shipped filename 'Antibiograms_ena_sra-analysis_20221119-2217.csv'. At Stage 1 no env_capture_class (A/B/C) may be assigned; on prose alone these read as unpinned external references.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the AMRFinderPlus tool version + database release (e.g. 2024-xx-xx.1) and the CheckM2 database version in the Methods and in the FTP release manifest; record a harvest date (or a frozen copy / DOI) for each of the nine source databases so the aggregation is re-derivable to a fixed snapshot.

gaps.where: Steps C8, C9, C10 - the entire genome assembly, QC and annotation arm
gaps.missing: The genomic arm of the resource is externalised to sub-pipelines that live outside the author repository (the AllTheBacteria collaboration for assembly, mettannotator for annotation) and is described in a single five-sentence Methods subsection (2.5). No invocation configuration, no Nextflow profile or params file, no sample sheet, no per-genome provenance table distinguishing ENA-submitted from newly-assembled genomes, and no accession for the assemblies the paper says are 'available via the European Nucleotide Archive'. The Leonardini/CABBAGE repository covers only the R-based tabular aggregation; nothing in it drives the genome side.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the mettannotator run configuration (params file / Nextflow profile / sample sheet) and the CheckM2 invocation alongside the FTP release, cite the AllTheBacteria release identifier used, and give the ENA project accession under which the CABBAGE assemblies were deposited.

gaps.where: Step C11 (CABBAGE vs ATLAS comparison, Figure 4b and the OR = 1.6 headline statistic); also Figures 2, 3, 4a
gaps.missing: No analysis or figure code is deposited. The repository README enumerates only extraction and preprocessing scripts plus Replication.R; nothing corresponds to the logistic regression, the Fisher exact tests with FDR adjustment across 103 pathogen-antibiotic pairs, the UpSet plot (Figure 2a / Supplementary Figure S1), the geographic aggregation (Figure 3a) or the resistance-frequency bars (Figure 4a). The paper also has no 'Code Availability' section at all - the only code statement is an in-line clause in Methods 2.1 covering the extraction scripts, and its scope does not reach the results analyses.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Code Availability section, and commit the figure/statistics scripts (with the exact filtering used: >=100 entries per pair, 2004-2023 restriction, original-source rather than updated phenotypes) to the same tagged release.

gaps.where: Step C5 (curation), and by extension the C4/C7 boundary
gaps.missing: The curation stage is explicitly partly manual - 'Only those entries that were inconsistent or conflicted have been manually curated', 'manually checked against the original data sources', 'conflicting entries that could not be resolved by checking the original sources were also excluded' - and PrepareTables.R is described by the README as containing 'semi-manual scripts'. No decision log, no exclusion ledger and no per-entry curation-reason field is described in the paper, so the manual judgements are not replayable and an independent re-run cannot converge on the same 170,750-isolate / 1.7M-entry object even with the scripts in hand.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship the curation decision ledger (excluded entry ID, reason code, resolving source) as a data file in the release, and add a per-entry provenance/curation-flag column to the distributed CABBAGE tables.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C2 (source coverage) and the database release as a whole
gaps.missing: The paper does not enumerate, in the main text, the 89 publications comprising the literature-derived arm, nor the per-database access dates; those are pushed to Supplementary Tables S2/S3 and the Supplementary Methods. The repository contains AllFoundPapers and NewlyFoundPapers listings, which partly closes this, but the mapping from source publication to the final BioSample set is not published as a single provenance table, so an entry in the released database cannot generally be traced back to the exact source table it came from without re-running the scripts.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a source-provenance table (source id -> source type -> accession/PMID/DOI -> harvest date -> n entries contributed) as part of the FTP release.

gaps.where: Step C11 (ATLAS comparator) and the isolate-level metadata retrieved from live NCBI/ENA services in C3
gaps.missing: The ATLAS dataset is used as the paper's key bias comparator but is not given an accession, DOI, version or download date; it is cited only through reference [17]. ATLAS is distributed under registration (Vivli), which is a legitimate but gated path, and the paper documents no access route, so the comparator arm is not directly re-fetchable from the paper alone. Similarly the BioSample-based metadata back-fill in C3 depends on live NCBI/ENA record state, which drifts, and no query date is recorded.
gaps.how_to_close: State the ATLAS version and download date (and the access route) in the Methods; record the date on which BioSample metadata were harvested, or ship the harvested metadata snapshot in the release.
